competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: global_live_discovery.dart header: 'liveSessionsProvider calls /realtime/sessions?scope=me, which returns sessions the viewer is a participant or member of. This is NOT a true cross-institution global feed'.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: A discovery surface that can only show what you already belong to is a recent-items list. Materially strengthens F081 and F097.
competitiveDeficiencies.interpretationFlag: Client-derived. Recommend Stage 2 confirm whether a global Live index is intended to exist.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Messaging lacks the modern baseline: edit, delete, reactions, search, emoji, typing, delivery truth, pagination
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: WG001, WG002, WG003, WG004, WG007, WG008, WG009, WG013, WG016 all NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Client corroboration: no ScrollController or cursor call in conversation_screen.dart; 'emoji' appears only in meeting_live_room_screen.dart; no typing indicator anywhere.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: Edit and delete are baseline in WhatsApp, Teams, Slack, X DMs and LinkedIn messaging. Their absence reads as an unfinished product on the very first send.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Attention that lies
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: F032 'Unread badges lie after viewing — undermines trust in every list'. F033 'call history is effectively unreadable'. F034 self-actor rows. F030/F031 'Not harmless'. Eight parallel attention surfaces per DR1.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: One badge, one meaning, cleared by reading. Universal. Aura has eight surfaces and a badge that does not clear.
competitiveDeficiencies.note: These ARE bugs, but fixing them individually still leaves eight surfaces. The deficiency survives the bug fix.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Refresh loses the user
competitiveDeficiencies.severity: HIGH — first-use credibility, encountered by every user
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: F059, F061, F062, F063, F064, F066, F067, F068, F070, F113 — destination, profile edits, composition, institution routes, meetings; F068 permanent spinner.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: Refresh-safety is table stakes on web. This is the cheapest large credibility win available.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Authoring surface below the long-form market
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: F025 raw markdown shown to the author, F026 title paste oversizing, F027 draft lost on refresh, F121 expiring signed URL baked into durable markdown (published images 404), F131 published cover deleted by the reaper.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: Medium / Substack / Notion / LinkedIn articles. Also a DURABILITY claim failure, not only a UX one.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Accessibility never audited anywhere in the product
competitiveDeficiencies.severity: MEDIUM-HIGH — institutional adoption blocker, legal exposure
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: WG015 'Never audited anywhere in this work' (WEAK_SINGLE_SOURCE). Client corroboration: 14 Semantics() usages across 571 Dart files, in 7 files, none of them Conversation, Articles, Live, Discover or any composer.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: Public institutions, universities and government buyers commonly require WCAG/VPAT statements. An unaudited product cannot answer the questionnaire at all.
competitiveDeficiencies.note: The client corroboration converts WG015 from a WEAK single-source assertion into a code-verifiable one. This matters because WG015 is otherwise a lone unauthorized row.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Confidentiality is untrue at the storage boundary
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: F138 CONFIRMED SECURITY ARCHITECTURE DEFECT (one bucket, every object written to the same public prefix; 'private' enforced by withholding the URL). F126 private DM attachments stay PUBLIC and GET /media/:id/url returns a permanent public URL to any caller. F129 correspondence path bypasses presign entirely. F127 no magic-byte validation. F132 GPS EXIF published verbatim. F135 viewer IP leakage. F137 no media moderation or scanning of any kind.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: This is the section of an institutional security review Aura currently fails on paper.
competitiveDeficiencies.note: F138 is the reason app-level fixes are insufficient: the §12 contract itself promoted RIC-C5 governed delivery to a SECURITY stage, and Stage-0 records C5 governed delivery as a security PREREQUISITE, never a bucket toggle.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Group calling unproven at four parties with an unmeasured ceiling
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: F073 late/missing fourth video frame, root cause UNKNOWN. F108 mesh bounded, CEILING NEVER MEASURED. F109 mesh not the long-term architecture, NO ENFORCEMENT. F110/F111 SFU assessment and its scope both unwritten.
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: Teams/Zoom/Meet. An institution will test a 6-person call before adopting.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Native binaries in the field are defective and cannot be re-observed without a release
competitiveDeficiencies.severity: MEDIUM-HIGH — credibility of anyone who already installed
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: F071 BLOCKED; both shared-code fixes post-date the released binaries; VD-032 requires a founder-triggered store release before the defect can even be re-observed. F072 group calls ring as individual.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: The canonical surface is the least capable surface
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: Client-derived: rich_paste_field.dart is imported by five legacy/demolition-listed composers and NOT by conversation_screen.dart; AuraMediaViewer and MediaSaveService are used by feed/post cards and NOT by Conversation (consistent with F125).
competitiveDeficiencies.competitiveFrame: Standardising on the least capable implementation means every future improvement is a re-implementation rather than an adoption.
competitiveDeficiencies.interpretationFlag: Structural interpretation of import graphs. Offered for Stage 2 scrutiny.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: No evidenced first-run journey standard
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: No obligation among VD-001..VD-082 has sign-up, sign-in, account recovery, onboarding or first-session quality as its subject. PD-2 has zero issued findings and an OPEN structural disposition.

competitiveDeficiencies.title: Meetings held to an older bar than the rest of the product
competitiveDeficiencies.evidence: F112 Meetings owes the equivalent validation, intact and unstarted. RC-C6's 3,890 duplicated presentation lines untouched; 0 of 5 shared realtime widgets consumed.
competitiveDeficiencies.protectionNote: Stated WITHOUT proposing any change to the Meetings protected boundary, which X7 records as consistently asserted across four authorities.

wgMapping.title: Message edit
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: A user cannot correct their own words. ConversationMessage.editedAt exists in schema but there is no API and no UI — the product models the concept and refuses to expose it.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation & Messaging Core (message authority). Stage-0 records its associated stage as RIC-E2 'Conversation as FIRST COMPLETE REFERENCE'.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — inseparable. Message mutability changes message truth, attention truth, timeline truth and moderation truth simultaneously. Retrofitting edit onto a reconstructed message surface later means reopening the same authority.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY COMPETITIVE CAPABILITY. Baseline in every comparison product.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F019 (rich/selectable text — edit re-renders the same body)
F123/F124 (message body truth already misused as a UI flag; edit multiplies the damage if body truth is not fixed first)
F032 (attention/read truth must not resurrect on edit)
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: Every message sent in the interim is permanently uncorrectable; user-visible immaturity on the first send.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: LOW-MEDIUM. The column exists. Risk concentrates in attention re-notification semantics (RC-C4 territory, not started) and in whether an edited message re-enters unread. Must not create a second attention path.

wgMapping.title: Message delete/retract
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: deletedAt / deletedReason exist and are HONOURED IN READS, but nothing can create them. The read path already believes in deletion; the write path does not exist.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation, then shared. Reuses moderation + message authority. RIC-E2.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES. Also touches S2 (deleting a message with an attachment must interact with retention truth — F140, F142, F143) and moderation (F023).
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY. Retraction is a safety capability, not a convenience: it is how a user limits harm from a mis-sent message.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F023 report/moderation
F140 legacy MessageAttachment media invisible to the reaper
F142 cleanup authority omits authoritative reference structures
F143 storage-object aliasing
F126 conversation media visibility
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: A user who mis-sends confidential material to the wrong conversation has no recourse. Given F126/F138, that material is additionally publicly addressable. The delay risk here is a real-world harm risk, not a feature-parity risk.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM-HIGH — deletion that frees storage objects intersects directly with the unresolved F143 aliasing defect (production holds 10 duplicate/canonical pairs where deleting one row frees an object another row still addresses). Sequencing matters.

wgMapping.title: Per-message delivery/read truth
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: Only a per-human read cursor exists; there is no sent/delivered/read state per message.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: Jointly S1 Conversation and S5 Attention. Stage-0 records associatedChapter RC-C4 (established by evidence, explicitly NOT the RIC C4 stage).
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES for S5 — delivery truth and attention truth are the same trust surface. Building it inside S1 alone would create a second read-state authority, which RC-C4's enforcement list explicitly gates against ('independent badge semantics', 'competing reconciliation').
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY EVENTUALLY, but genuinely coupled — the issuance recommendation 'LATER (C4 coupling)' is well-founded and I concur on the coupling (not on any authorization).
materiallyInteractingFindings: F032 unread persists after viewing
F033 call facts projected generically
F034 self-actor notifications
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: MODERATE. Users tolerate absent read receipts far better than LYING ones — and F032 shows Aura currently has the lying kind. Fixing F032 is more urgent than adding WG003.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: HIGH IF DONE EARLY — a per-message state model built before the Attention Authority exists is precisely the 'temporary version of an authority already scheduled for reconstruction' that the frozen C10 invariant warns against by analogy.
wgMapping.provenanceCaution: WEAK_SINGLE_SOURCE — this row exists in exactly one assistant message. Do not build a major architectural conclusion on it alone; the corroboration here is the independent F032/F033 evidence, not the WG row.

wgMapping.title: Large-history pagination
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: The backend 'before' cursor EXISTS; the frontend never calls it — no ScrollController, loads a single page forever.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — this is a correctness and performance property of the conversation surface, not a feature bolted onto it.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY. Independently corroborated in the released client: conversation_screen.dart contains no ScrollController, no loadMore, no hasMore, no cursor call. This is one of only two WG items I could verify directly against code.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F011/F125 (an attachment sent before the loaded page is currently unreachable by ANY path — this is what makes WG010's 'unrecoverable once scrolled past' true)
F059 (destination continuity — restoring a destination into a truncated history is a partial restore)
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: Compounds with time and usage. Every day of use makes more of every conversation unreachable, and it silently invalidates any claim that Aura is a durable communication record.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: LOW. The API already exists. Main risk is scroll-anchor jitter and interaction with realtime message insertion.
wgMapping.wouldItBeGoodEnoughWithoutIt: NO — categorically. A messenger without history is not a messenger.

wgMapping.title: Failed-send truth + retry
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: Failure is a transient toast; THE MESSAGE IS SIMPLY LOST.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation -> shared composer (S2 composition territory).
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES. RC-C0 already froze the RETRY semantic CTA family and the failed/sending product-state vocabulary — the authority to express this exists and is unconsumed here.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY. Silent data loss on the product's primary action. This is arguably the most severe WG item on a pure harm basis.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F063 compose systems continuity (a failed send whose text is also lost on navigation is a double loss)
F124 empty-text ellipsis sentinel (message body truth is already unreliable)
WG013 offline queue is the same failure mode via a different cause
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: HIGH AND SILENT. Users do not report messages they do not know failed; they conclude the recipient ignored them. This damages the relationship, not just the product.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: LOW-MEDIUM. Needs a local pending/failed message representation, which must not become a second message store — coordinate with WG006/F063/F070's persistence mechanism, per the founder's explicit instruction on WG006.

wgMapping.title: Per-conversation draft persistence
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: Shared composer (S2), consuming the continuity authority (S7).
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — and the founder already ruled on HOW: 'Coordinate this with F063/F070. Do not create another unrelated persistence mechanism.' That instruction is preserved verbatim in Stage-0 and is the single most important sequencing constraint in the WG register.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F063 compose systems continuity (RC7/RC8)
F070 draft identity absent from URL (RC7)
F027 article draft lost on refresh
F065 RC1 session hint — the gating root cause
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: MEDIUM. But the delay risk is inverted here: implementing it EARLY and SEPARATELY is the larger risk, because it would create exactly the parallel persistence mechanism the founder forbade.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM — the risk is architectural, not data. Storage-axis note: the co-token 'RC7' in the issuance row is C_AXIS_AMBIGUOUS per Stage-0 (written neither as RC-C7 nor RIC-C7) and separately RC7 is used as a ROOT-CAUSE LABEL in the refresh-continuity audit. Do not resolve this by token shape.

wgMapping.title: In-conversation search
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: No endpoint, no UI; unusable at scale.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation. A search repository already exists to reuse.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: PARTIALLY — the retrieval half can follow, but the surface's information architecture should reserve the affordance during reconstruction rather than acquire it as a patch.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY AT SCALE, NOT AT TODAY'S SCALE. Honest read: with WG004 absent, in-conversation search would today be the ONLY way to reach an old message — which perversely raises its urgency.
materiallyInteractingFindings: WG004 pagination (search is a substitute retrieval path)
WG010 media gallery (the same 'I cannot find what was sent' complaint)
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: LOW-MEDIUM NOW, HIGH LATER. Grows strictly with history volume.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM — backend indexing work; must respect F126/F138 visibility so search never surfaces content the viewer may not access.

wgMapping.title: Message reactions
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: No lightweight acknowledgement primitive. Explicitly recorded as DISTINCT from Live reactions (F091) — a contrast, not a dependency.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES, IF DONE — reactions change message rendering, attention semantics ('did a reaction earn a notification?') and read-state, so bolting them on later is a three-system change.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY FOR RETENTION, NOT FOR FUNCTION. Reactions are the cheapest social-affordance-per-engineering-hour in modern messaging and are universal in the comparison set. Also directly reduces low-value message volume, which improves attention quality.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F091 Live reactions (distinct, but a shared reaction vocabulary would be a genuine reuse opportunity)
F034 self-actor notifications (a reaction system built before attention truth would multiply self-actor noise)
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: LOW ON CORRECTNESS, MEDIUM ON RETENTION.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM — introduces a per-message aggregate that attention must not double-count.

wgMapping.title: Typing/presence indicators
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: Common expectation, but the issuance row itself flags that it 'arguably conflicts with passive presence is not attention'. The issuance recommendation was FOUNDER CALL and the founder authorized it explicitly under ephemeral-interaction doctrine.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — and it is a genuine DOCTRINE INTERSECTION, not just a feature. C1-4 froze 'Presence is the person'; RC-C4 gates against 'unread-as-universal-attention'. Typing is ephemeral interaction signal, NOT presence and NOT attention. Building it outside a reconstruction would risk conflating all three.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F052/F053/F116 canonical identity consumption (a typing indicator names a person and must use canonical identity, not an ad-hoc resolution)
C1-4 presence doctrine
GAP-1 Availability Off — a user who has turned availability off must not leak typing state
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: LOW ON CORRECTNESS. Conversation feels dead without it, which affects perceived liveness more than function.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM — the real risk is doctrinal contamination (typing treated as presence, or presence treated as attention), not technical. Client corroboration: no isTyping/typingIndicator symbol exists anywhere in the released client, so there is no legacy behaviour to preserve.

wgMapping.title: Media/files gallery per conversation
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: Attachments are unrecoverable once scrolled past.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S2 Rich media presentation, surfaced in S1 Conversation. Reuses the media authority.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — a gallery is the natural PROOF that a media system is coherent. It is the surface where thumbnails, kinds, names and save paths all have to be real at once.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY FOR INSTITUTIONAL USEFULNESS. 'Where is that PDF she sent me' is the single most common institutional retrieval task in a messaging product.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F058 — Stage-0 records an EXPLICIT blocking relation: 'F058 (R2 CORS) blocks visual completion of F051, F052, F056, and WG010'. Stage 0 did NOT promote WG010 to BLOCKED and neither do I.
F136 no thumbnail generation — thumbUrl is the FULL-RESOLUTION original and is null for video/audio/document, so a gallery today would be a slow grid of broken tiles
F125 no viewer and no save in conversation
F016 media-kind honesty
WG004 pagination (the underlying retrieval problem)
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: MEDIUM-HIGH AND COMPOUNDING — every day of use buries more content.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: LOW ARCHITECTURALLY, but it is a DEPENDENT capability: implementing it before F058, F136 and F126 are resolved would produce a gallery that is slow, broken and potentially leaks. This is the clearest case in the WG register where sequencing behind findings is a product decision, not a bureaucratic one.
wgMapping.provenanceCaution: WEAK_SINGLE_SOURCE for the WG row; the blocking relation to F058 is separately and explicitly evidenced.

wgMapping.title: Forward/share message to another conversation
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: No way to move information between conversations. The primitive already exists: internal-reference hydration.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation, reusing the internal reference service.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — and unusually cheap, because F017's internal-ref card already renders live.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY COMPETITIVELY (universal in WhatsApp/Slack/Teams), and it is also a QUIET GROWTH MECHANIC: forwarding is how content travels inside an institution.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F017 internal Aura-link hydration (PARTIALLY_VALIDATED — the /p/ backfill/skip-guard gap would be inherited by every forward of an older message)
F126/F138 — forwarding an attachment across a visibility boundary is a privacy decision, not a copy operation
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM — the visibility question above is genuinely hard and must not be answered by accident. Forwarding must not launder a RESTRICTED object into a PUBLIC conversation.

wgMapping.title: Block boundary inside Conversation
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: Report exists; block/unblock semantics are not surfaced in Conversation. Reuses the compliance authority.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation, consuming the canonical blocking authority established by C2-R1.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — C2-R1 froze 'BLOCKING OUTRANKS FOLLOW/RELATIONSHIP/MESSAGING ELIGIBILITY' and the C2 §6 forensic found D2 'blocking does not stop DMs' as a SAFETY defect, since resolved and certified. The authority is now correct; the USER-FACING SURFACE for it inside Conversation is what WG012 names.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY — SAFETY. This is not a parity feature. A user experiencing harassment must be able to stop it from inside the conversation where it is happening, not by navigating to a profile.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F023 report/moderation (IMPLEMENTED_NOT_LIVE_CERTIFIED — the report sheet is wired but the live journey has NEVER been run)
C2-R1/R5 blocking precedence
F137 no media moderation of any kind
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: HIGH ON A HARM BASIS, LOW ON A VOLUME BASIS. I judge this the most UNDER-RATED row in the WG register: it is recommended 'LATER' and marked WEAK_SINGLE_SOURCE, yet it is the only WG item whose absence has a direct personal-safety consequence. FLAGGED FOR STAGE 2 as a candidate re-reading of its priority — NOT as an authorization request.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: LOW — the authority already exists and is certified; this is surfacing, not building.
wgMapping.provenanceCaution: WEAK_SINGLE_SOURCE for the WG row; the underlying blocking authority and the D2 safety defect are separately and STRONGLY evidenced in C2.

wgMapping.title: Offline queue + reconnect replay
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: Sends during a connectivity blip VANISH.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: Shared / platform. Reuses realtime reconnect machinery.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — same failure class as WG005 (failed-send truth) and the same persistence question as WG006/F063. Three different rows describing one missing durability layer.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY ON MOBILE. Mobile networks blip constantly; this is not an edge case there.
materiallyInteractingFindings: WG005 failed-send truth
WG006/F063/F070 draft persistence
F117 refresh as a platform contract
F046 call lost after freeze/refresh (same durability instinct, different domain)
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: MEDIUM-HIGH ON MOBILE, LOW ON DESKTOP WEB.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM-HIGH — an offline queue that replays without idempotency causes duplicate sends, which is a worse failure than the one it fixes. Must be designed with WG005 as one mechanism.

wgMapping.title: Keyboard/desktop discipline (Enter vs Shift+Enter, shortcuts)
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: The composer has a key handler for PASTE ONLY. There is no send/newline discipline and no shortcut vocabulary.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: Split by evidence: composer behaviour sits with S2 composition; platform behaviour sits with S12 cross-platform (RC-C9 explicitly lists 'keyboard' in its build scope, and RC-C5's Composition Authority explicitly lists 'keyboard' and 'accessibility').
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES — BOTH. This is a genuine two-owner capability and Stage-0 already shows the same shape for drag/drop ('jointly owned C5 + C9').
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY FOR DESKTOP CREDIBILITY. RC-C9's own governing rule is 'DESKTOP IS NOT WEB WITH A WIDER VIEWPORT'; keyboard discipline is the most legible expression of that rule. Aura ships MSIX; power users on desktop judge a messenger in the first thirty seconds by whether Enter sends.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F013 clipboard paste (the one key handler that DOES exist, and it has never been exercised live)
F019 rich/selectable text (selection and copy are keyboard behaviours)
WG015 accessibility — keyboard navigability IS an accessibility requirement, not merely a power-user nicety
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: MEDIUM. Also accumulates: every new surface built without keyboard discipline is another surface to retrofit.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: LOW-MEDIUM. Changing Enter behaviour on an existing composer IS a user-visible behaviour change, but the frozen product standard explicitly notes there is no installed base whose legacy behaviour must be preserved at the cost of quality.

wgMapping.title: Accessibility pass (semantics, labels, contrast, screen reader)
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: 'Never audited anywhere in this work.' Scope recorded as PLATFORM, authority to reuse recorded as the design system.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: PLATFORM-WIDE — it has no single owning system by nature, which is exactly why it has no home and keeps being deferred.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: IT MUST BE INSIDE EVERY RECONSTRUCTION, NOT A CHAPTER OF ITS OWN. Accessibility retrofitted as a late pass is the single most reliably-abandoned item in software. RC-C0's precedent shows the mechanism that would work: the FD-13 pattern of zero-tolerance rules plus RATCHETS. A Semantics-coverage ratchet is directly analogous to the G2/G3/G4/G5/G7 ratchets C0 already froze — a technically sound, deliberately migratable improvement of exactly the kind the frozen product standard says to consider NOW.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY — AND IT IS AN INSTITUTIONAL ADOPTION BLOCKER, not a nicety. Public institutions, universities, healthcare and government procurement routinely require WCAG conformance or a VPAT. An unaudited product cannot answer the questionnaire at all, which removes Aura from consideration before any feature is compared.
materiallyInteractingFindings: WG014 keyboard discipline (keyboard navigability is an accessibility requirement)
RC-C0's product-state vocabulary and RC-C5's Composition Authority both list accessibility explicitly in scope
F016/F125/F136 — an image with no alt text and no accessible name is inaccessible regardless of how well it renders
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: HIGH AND COMPOUNDING. Cost grows linearly with surface count; Aura currently has 571 Dart files and 14 Semantics() usages.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: LOW TECHNICALLY. The risk is organisational: without a ratchet it will not hold.
wgMapping.provenanceCaution: The WG row is WEAK_SINGLE_SOURCE. HOWEVER: I independently corroborated it against the released client — 14 Semantics() occurrences across 7 files out of 571 Dart files, none in Conversation, Articles, Live, Discover or any composer. That converts the claim from a single assertion into a code-verifiable fact. This is the one WEAK-provenance WG row on which I am willing to rest a strong conclusion, and only because of that independent corroboration.

wgMapping.title: Participant management beyond LEAVE
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: Schema comments say v1 exit is LEAVE only; there is no removal and no stewardship. Issuance recommendation was 'LATER (needs doctrine)'.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation, reusing the invitation authority. Note that Stage-0 records the Invitation System canon stating explicitly 'Invitation is NOT a C7 feature' — so the reusable authority is NOT where the original charter placed it.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: YES, AND IT NEEDS DOCTRINE FIRST. 'Who may remove whom from a conversation' is a governance question, and C1-1 froze that governance is never a delegable capability. This cannot be answered by implementation.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: NECESSARY FOR GROUP CREDIBILITY. A group conversation someone cannot be removed from is not usable for institutional work — a departed employee stays in the room forever.
materiallyInteractingFindings: F009 grow 1:1 -> group via Add People (LIVE_CERTIFIED — the product can ADD but not REMOVE, an asymmetry users notice immediately)
F055 group identity ordering (removal changes the joinedAt-derived order)
F056 group avatar treatment (removal changes the composite avatar)
C1-1 governance never delegable
wgMapping.riskOfDelaying: MEDIUM NOW, HIGH AS GROUPS PERSIST. The asymmetry with F009 makes it more visible than its usage frequency suggests.
wgMapping.migrationOrRegressionRisk: MEDIUM — removal semantics interact with message history visibility (does a removed participant retain access to prior messages?) which is a doctrine question with F126/F138 consequences.

wgMapping.title: Pin/save messages
wgMapping.motivatingDeficiency: 'No evidence of need yet.' The issuance recommendation was 'REJECT for now' — recorded by Stage-0 as an ASSISTANT recommendation, NOT a founder ruling. Stage-0 explicitly does NOT record it as RETIRED or REJECTED, and neither do I.
wgMapping.naturallyOwningSystem: S1 Conversation. relatedSystemOrDomain and existingAuthorityToReuse are both NOT_RECORDED (dashes in source) — this row is the thinnest in the register.
wgMapping.insideReconstructionOfThatSystem: IF IT IS EVER DONE, YES — pinning is a per-conversation surface property.
wgMapping.optionalOrNecessary: OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENT. I concur with the issuance assessment on evidence: no finding, no founder observation and no user report motivates it. I note honestly that pinning is common in Slack and Teams, so it may re-emerge as an institutional-usability request later; it should not be deleted from the register on that basis.
materiallyInteractingFindings: WG007 in-conversation search and WG010 media gallery address the same underlying 'I cannot find it again' need more generally, and would likely reduce the demand for pinning

wgMappingSummary.wg018: RESERVED / UNISSUED — treated as never issued throughout. No new WG identifier is minted by this analysis.

myProductAssessmentIndependentOfAuthoriz.note: This is a PRODUCT ASSESSMENT of competitive necessity ONLY. It is not an authorization, not a priority order, not a recommendation to implement, and does NOT reclassify any founder authorization decision. Authorization is founder-only authority.

wgMappingSummary.structuralObservation: Every one of the 17 WG rows names a capability that belongs INSIDE the reconstruction of an existing system. Not one of them is a standalone feature. This is the strongest argument in the evidence against ever creating a separate WG implementation phase — and it matches the record that the six authorized items were already 'folded into the Rich Content chapter's sequencing rather than implemented as isolated patches'.

unmappedSurfaceAnalysis.governingConstraint: CR-R4 ruled all five UNMAPPED_TO_RC, explicitly NOT force-assigned and explicitly NOT automatically an architectural defect. Nothing below assigns ownership. This is my PRODUCT-LENS reading only; final ownership is Stage 4.

surfaces.name: Platform Administration
surfaces.productReading: The lowest acquisition consequence of the five and the highest OPERATIONAL consequence. Its users are internal. Its measured debt is real (11 files / 34 G5 sites, the largest single withdrawal from RC-C1's original 42) and VD-028 records the ENTIRE /admin workspace was fail-open on route classification until the C3 gate found it — an authority surface with no auth classification is a governance risk, not a polish item.
surfaces.worldClassTest: Would an operator trust it? Unassessed. No finding, no obligation, no evidence of quality assessment exists.
surfaces.acquisitionConsequence: INDIRECT — poor admin tooling slows every institutional onboarding, which is a growth cost rather than a conversion cost.
surfaces.myView: Belongs inside a reconstruction of whatever owns institutional authority presentation, because C1's capability projection is what it must consume. NOT a standalone chapter in my reading. STATED AS OPINION.

surfaces.name: Authentication & Account Entry
surfaces.productReading: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL UNMAPPED SURFACE AND THE LEAST EXAMINED THING IN THE ENTIRE BASELINE. 100% of users pass through it. It has ZERO issued findings, ZERO dedicated validation obligations, only 3 G5 sites, and DECISIONS.md records its STRUCTURAL DISPOSITION REMAINS OPEN.
surfaces.worldClassTest: FAILS THE TEST BY DEFAULT — not because it is bad, but because nobody has looked. Sign-up conversion, error recovery, password reset, session restoration and the public-to-authenticated transition are the highest-leverage acquisition surface in any consumer product.
surfaces.acquisitionConsequence: DIRECT AND MAXIMAL. F103/F104 (sign-up preserves intent, auth returns to the SAME Live) are the conversion moment of the entire Live acquisition thesis and both are OPEN, and both are gated by F065/RC1 which lives in the same territory.
surfaces.myView: The absence of a single finding here is more likely evidence of an unexamined surface than of a healthy one. Stage 2 should treat 'zero findings' as a signal to LOOK, not as reassurance. STATED AS INTERPRETATION.

surfaces.name: Support surface
surfaces.productReading: Deliberately NOT assigned to RC-C9 and ownership-undetermined. The released client shows a scattered support presence: features/support/ (agent screen, admin console, case list, chat bubble, quick chips), features/monetization/presentation/support_screen.dart, screens/supporters_hub_screen.dart and screens/support_fallback_screen.dart. Note the NAME COLLISION: 'support' means both customer help AND financial supporters/monetization in this codebase.
surfaces.worldClassTest: Unassessed. A vocabulary collision on a user-facing word is exactly the class of problem C0's Product Language Authority exists to prevent, and this one appears to have survived C0.
surfaces.acquisitionConsequence: INSTITUTIONAL — 'how do we get help' is a procurement question and an SLA question.
surfaces.myView: The vocabulary collision is a concrete, checkable observation worth raising at Stage 2 independently of ownership. Client-derived; flagged.

surfaces.name: Settings / Personal Controls
surfaces.productReading: UNCHARTERED, and it holds a control the doctrine declares REQUIRED with the implementation owner explicitly UNASSIGNED (Availability Off). Stage-0 additionally records that the earlier 'C4 Settings' shorthand was RECLASSIFIED as continuity shorthand, i.e. it never really had a home.
surfaces.worldClassTest: FAILS. Every comparison product gives users granular control over notifications, visibility and privacy. Aura's notification preference authority is an obligation owned by an unstarted chapter, and its availability control has no owner at all.
surfaces.acquisitionConsequence: RETENTION AND TRUST. Users who cannot control interruption churn or mute. Users who cannot control visibility do not trust the product with their presence.
surfaces.myView: This is the unmapped surface most likely to be quietly load-bearing for retention, and it is also where GAP-1, WG015 accessibility settings, WG009 typing/presence and RC-C4's notification preferences all converge. STATED AS OPINION.

surfaces.name: Long-Form Publishing (Articles)
surfaces.productReading: CARRIES ITS OWN PRESERVED CONTRADICTION, which I carry forward and do not resolve: DECISIONS.md records NO CHAPTER NUMBER ASSIGNED awaiting founder dependency placement, yet Articles SHIPPED and F024 is LIVE_CERTIFIED. A capability that is simultaneously unchartered and in production.
surfaces.worldClassTest: FAILS on authoring (F025, F026, F027) and on DURABILITY (F121 published images 404 after signature expiry; F131 published covers deleted by the reaper).
surfaces.acquisitionConsequence: HIGH AND UNDER-APPRECIATED. Public articles are the most shareable, most linkable and most search-visible artifact Aura produces. A decaying public archive is a permanent negative signal that outlives any fix.
surfaces.myView: The durability defects matter more than the ownership question. An unchartered capability that works is a governance issue; a published archive that silently rots is a product-thesis failure. STATED AS OPINION.
surfaces.contradictionCarriedForward: RC-C11 records that a release gate enumerating C0-C10 has no declared home for it. Preserved, not resolved.

unmappedSurfaceAnalysis.crossCuttingObservation: Four of the five unmapped surfaces (PD-2 auth, GAP-1 settings, SupportScreen, PD-1 admin) share one property: they are the surfaces a user meets when something needs to be CONTROLLED or FIXED, rather than when something is being CREATED or COMMUNICATED. The RC roadmap is organised almost entirely around creation and communication. That is a coherent explanation for why these five have no home, and it is offered as a hypothesis for Stage 2, not as a defect claim — CR-R4 explicitly forbids treating unmapped status as automatically defective.

contradictions.subject: F043 — Timer before establishment
contradictions.stage0Record: CR-O1: the master register row records PARTIALLY_VALIDATED while the same message lists it among items that cannot honestly be called LIVE_CERTIFIED.
contradictions.myReading: IMPLEMENTATION STATE VS CERTIFICATION STATE — STATED EXPLICITLY AS AN INTERPRETATION, NOT A RESOLUTION. The founder ruling shipped (b25b554) and was certified; a subsequent answeredAt-only refinement (b401398) is unverified. Both statements can be simultaneously true of different commits. VD-014's owed proof ('re-verify Ready-to-join shows no clock') is consistent with that reading.
contradictions.resolutionStatus: NOT RESOLVED. Carried forward unchanged. Evidence is sufficient to OFFER the interpretation and insufficient to CLOSE the conflict; the two states may also genuinely disagree.
contradictions.productConsequence: A call timer that starts before establishment tells the user the call connected when it did not. Whichever reading is correct, the user-facing obligation is identical and cheap to verify.

contradictions.subject: F051 — Avatar missing in chat
contradictions.stage0Record: CR-O2: register row PARTIALLY_VALIDATED vs the same report's 'previously called fixed & deployed' list.
contradictions.myReading: IMPLEMENTATION STATE VS CERTIFICATION STATE — OFFERED AS INTERPRETATION. The thread-header avatar is live; the Messages-list avatars are deployed (b401398) but unverified. VD-019's owed proof is exactly 'verify Messages-list avatars deployed in b401398'. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT reading is equally available and I do not dismiss it: F058's R2 CORS block means avatars may be deployed in code and still not RENDER on web, in which case 'deployed' and 'not working' are both literally true and the conflict is not about certification at all.
contradictions.resolutionStatus: NOT RESOLVED. Both readings preserved. The second reading materially changes what proof would settle it.
contradictions.productConsequence: Faceless people is a first-impression failure. Either reading points at F058 as the real gate.

contradictions.subject: F122 — Wire-kind inconsistency (canonical wireKind(document) returns 'IMAGE'; conversation_screen sends 'DOCUMENT')
contradictions.stage0Record: CR-O3: the frozen RIC stage C1 is documented as closing F122, but the C1 implementation checkpoint names only F127/F128/F130.
contradictions.myReading: SCOPE-DECLARATION VS SCOPE-EXECUTION MISMATCH — OFFERED AS INTERPRETATION, NOT A RESOLUTION. This is NOT cleanly 'implementation vs certification': the conflict is about whether the item was in the delivered scope at all, which is a different axis. VD-053 lists F122 alongside F127/F128/F130 as awaiting live certification of the content-truth authority, which weakly favours the 'in scope' reading, but the checkpoint's own omission is direct contrary evidence.
contradictions.resolutionStatus: NOT RESOLVED. Explicitly NOT collapsed into the implementation-vs-certification frame.
contradictions.productConsequence: Two messaging surfaces report different kinds for identical content, so any per-kind presentation model (F016) built on wireKind would be built on an inconsistent foundation. This makes F122 a PREREQUISITE of the document-presentation work, not a peer of it.

contradictions.subject: F139 — Identity media orphaned at upload and reaper-deletable
contradictions.carriedForwardState: DUAL READING PRESERVED — STRUCTURALLY_CLOSED_NOT_LIVE_CERTIFIED (backend register) vs OPEN (frontend §12 amendment), recorded THE SAME DAY with equal recency; neither supersedes.
contradictions.myReading: THIS ONE I DO READ AS IMPLEMENTATION STATE VS CERTIFICATION STATE, AND I SAY SO EXPLICITLY AS AN INTERPRETATION. VD-056 states the closure condition precisely: 'Structure landed (D-1, 4af75c5) but closure explicitly requires the migration applied AND identity reconciled in production.' Both records are then simultaneously accurate: the STRUCTURE is closed and the OUTCOME is open. VD-055 corroborates — migration 20260903000000_d1_identity_media_authority is COMMITTED AND NOT APPLIED.
contradictions.resolutionStatus: NOT RESOLVED — the interpretation is offered, the dual reading is preserved intact, and the founder-ratified conflict is not normalised. If Stage 2 accepts the interpretation it should record it as an accepted interpretation, not as a discovered fact.
contradictions.productConsequence: A user's profile photo can be deleted by a cleanup process while it is actively in use. If it fires, the visible result is a product that forgets people's faces — compounding F058. The risk is live in production until the migration deploys.

contradictions.subject: RC-C10 — Live (cross-repository)
contradictions.stage0Record: CR-O5. Reading A: OPEN — NOT STARTED (CURRENT_STATE.md:19, NEXT_WORK.md:101 'blocked until C0-C8 all stable', NEXT_WORK.md:121 'Explicitly NOT next: Live (C10)'). Reading B: SUBSTANTIALLY CONSTRUCTED OUTSIDE THE CHAPTER FRAME (origination correction FOUNDER-FROZEN 2026-08-17, backend commits 88179ee/d3981e5/fb9bfa1, viewer path, role authority, counts and state model implemented and partly live-verified).
contradictions.myReading: PRODUCT-LENS OBSERVATION ONLY, NOT AN ADJUDICATION: the two readings are separable by LAYER rather than by truth value. What exists is the SESSION MODEL (origination, escalation, roles, counts, admission). What does not exist is the LIVE PRODUCT (viewer experience F089-F095, public acquisition F097-F107, audience scale F108-F111). Reading A is accurate about the product; Reading B is accurate about the plumbing. I do NOT claim this resolves the conflict — the chapter's state is a governance fact, not a product fact, and the chapter also carries a frozen invariant (LIVE MUST NOT CREATE TEMPORARY VERSIONS OF AUTHORITIES ALREADY SCHEDULED FOR RECONSTRUCTION) whose status Stage 0 explicitly declined to adjudicate.
contradictions.productConsequence: The layer distinction matters for Stage 2 because it means Live's engineering progress and Live's product readiness are on different curves, and reporting either as 'Live status' would mislead.

OFFERED AS INTERPRETATION. It does not license merging them and I do not propose merging them.
